correctness.rationale: Exact spherical Fourier-Bessel decomposition reduces the infinite-dimensional normal operator to diagonal moments T_k. Standard Bessel derivative recurrence proves T_k-T_{k+1}=R J_{nu+k}J_{nu+k+1}; the three-term relation proves T_k-T_{k+2}=2(nu+k+1)J_{nu+k+1}^2≥0. Both parity chains then give top degree 0 or 1 with only 0/1 and 0/1/2 ties at noncommon Bessel zeros. Comparing the first excluded degrees yields an attained strictly positive gap in all four cases. Taylor expansions at simple neighboring-order zeros give the stated one-sided linear/quadratic laws. The checker independently verifies 756 finite cases without replacing universal proof.

value.rationale: Finite-aperture energy of Herglotz waves and conditioning away from optimal angular profiles are natural exact Fourier restriction questions. The theorem provides a complete all-radius, all-dimension equality classification, identifies infinitely many triple-mode resonances, and gives a sharp distance-to-extremizers coercivity constant that collapses quadratically on only one side of those resonances. This answers a natural structural/stability classification beyond a single numerical slice or an arbitrary isolated identity.
